topic.short_description: Alcoholism treatment drug repurposed for cancer therapy
topic.seo_title: Disulfiram in Cancer Research - Latest Studies & Findings | Your Cancer Breakthroughs
topic.seo_description: Explore Disulfiram cancer research and off-label use. Discover latest studies on this alcoholism drug repurposed for cancer therapy and treatment potential.
topic.seo_intro:
Disulfiram, commonly known as Antabuse, is a medication traditionally used to treat alcohol use disorder by creating an aversive reaction to alcohol consumption. However, emerging cancer research has identified potential anti-cancer properties in this established pharmaceutical compound, leading scientists to investigate its repurposing as a complementary cancer therapy. This shift represents an important trend in oncology research where older medications are being re-evaluated for novel applications in fighting cancer cells.

The scientific interest in Disulfiram for cancer treatment stems from its ability to inhibit aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) and copper metabolism, cellular processes that some cancer cells depend upon for survival and growth. Preclinical and early clinical studies suggest that Disulfiram may slow cancer progression and enhance the effectiveness of conventional treatments like chemotherapy. While research is still in its early to intermediate stages, the results have been promising enough to warrant continued investigation in multiple cancer types.

On this page, you'll find the latest peer-reviewed research articles examining Disulfiram's potential in cancer therapy, including mechanistic studies, laboratory findings, and early clinical trials. As with all off-label medication research, it's important to consult with your oncology team before considering any new treatment approaches. The articles below represent the most current scientific evidence available on this promising area of cancer research.

articles.title: Antitumor Activity of Sodium Selenite, Palbociclib, and Disulfiram Against Osteosarcoma and Rhabdomyosarcoma Cell Lines.
articles.hook: Sodium selenite, palbociclib, and disulfiram inhibit osteosarcoma and rhabdomyosarcoma growth
articles.summary: Three existing drugs—sodium selenite, palbociclib, and disulfiram—show promise against childhood bone and muscle cancers by stopping tumor growth and spread.

articles.title: Disulfiram/Copper Complex Induces Cytotoxicity in Pancreatic Cancer Cells and 5-Fluorouracil-Resistant Cells through Nuclear Factor E2-Related Factor-2 Suppression and Reactive Oxygen Species Modulation.
articles.hook: Disulfiram-copper complex kills chemotherapy-resistant pancreatic cancer cells
articles.summary: Disulfiram combined with copper kills pancreatic cancer cells, including those resistant to standard chemotherapy.

articles.title: CuET promotes cuproptosis and ferroptosis of lung cancer cells by interacting directly with polyunsaturated phospholipids.
articles.hook: CuET triggers cuproptosis and ferroptosis in...
articles.summary: Disulfiram's copper metabolite kills lung cancer cells by triggering two death pathways simultaneously: cuproptosis and ferroptosis.

articles.title: Off-label and repurposed use of disulfiram beyond alcohol dependence: A systematic review of clinical and preclinical evidence.
articles.hook: Disulfiram demonstrates anti-cancer activity in preclinical studies despite clinical trial obstacles
articles.summary: Disulfiram shows promise for cancer and other diseases, but clinical trials struggle with poor drug delivery, high toxicity, and recruitment challenges.

articles.title: CuET inhibits Ewing sarcoma of bone progression through modulation of the ESM1-MAPK/ERK signaling axis.
articles.hook: CuET inhibits Ewing sarcoma progression via...
articles.summary: CuET, a copper compound from disulfiram metabolism, inhibits Ewing sarcoma progression by blocking ESM1-MAPK/ERK signaling.

articles.title: A novel combination therapy for ER+ breast cancer suppresses drug resistance via an evolutionary double-bind.
articles.summary: Researchers found that combining chemotherapy with disulfiram in ER+ breast cancer forces resistant cells into an evolutionary trap, restoring drug sensitivity.

articles.title: ALDH1A1 is a potential novel target for treatment of ADPKD.
articles.hook: Disulfiram blocks ALDH1A1 to slow cyst growth...
articles.summary: Researchers found that blocking ALDH1A1 protein with disulfiram drug slows cyst growth in polycystic kidney disease mice.

articles.title: Aldehyde dehydrogenase 1 A1 regulates the transcription of PD-L1 and its targeting with disulfiram together with PD-L1 immunotherapy synergistically delays cyst growth in ADPKD.
articles.summary: Disulfiram combined with immunotherapy slows kidney cyst growth in polycystic kidney disease by targeting ALDH1A1.

articles.title: Repurposing disulfiram for ALDH-positive NSCLC: Network-based inhibition of EGFR, COX-2, and MAPK1.
articles.summary: Disulfiram effectively inhibits key cancer-promoting proteins in ALDH-positive non-small cell lung cancer, potentially overcoming drug resistance and treatment challenges.

articles.title: Disulfiram metabolite Cu(DDC)2 enhances radionuclide uptake in vivo revealing insights into tumoural ablation resistance.
articles.summary: A copper-containing derivative of disulfiram improved iodine uptake in tumors, potentially enhancing radioiodine treatment effectiveness for cancer patients.
